Drop anchor with a deliberately opposite guess. The country's outline gives more information than most players use on their first pass. Look at the coastline curvature before checking any other feature. How direction and distance clues narrow the shape

The arrow pointing northeast combined with a distance reading around 2,000 kilometers tells you something specific: you're looking for a country positioned southwest of your last guess. If you've been working through the puzzle already, that directional hint should confirm whether you're in the right hemisphere at least.

Distance percentages in Worldle work differently than raw mileage. A 78% match means the shape shares significant geographic features with the target—not that it's 78% of the distance away. Worldle's algorithm rewards geographic diversity. Two countries sharing a border will produce lower similarity scores than two countries with matching coastlines on opposite shores. The percentage measures shape and position similarity, not correctness. Two countries can share 85% geometric overlap yet occupy entirely different regions. Your guess might look almost identical to the answer on paper but sit thousands of kilometers away in reality.
